title: Sections separating points and tangent vectors give a closed immersion
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, $X$ a proper scheme over $k$, $\mathcal L$ an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module], and $V\subseteq H^0(X,\mathcal L)$ a $k$-subspace. Suppose (0) for every closed point $x\in X$ some $s\in V$ does not vanish at $x$ (equivalently, $V$ generates $\mathcal L$ [def-weil-pbc-generating-sections]); (1) for every pair of distinct closed points $x,y\in X$ some $s\in V$ vanishes at $x$ but not at $y$, and (2) for every closed point $x$ and every nonzero tangent vector $\theta\in T_{X/k,x}=\operatorname{Hom}_k(\mathfrak m_x/\mathfrak m_x^2,k)$ some $s\in V$ vanishes at $x$ and has nonzero first derivative along $\theta$. Then $V$ is finite-dimensional, and the morphism $\varphi_{\mathcal L,V}:X\to\mathbf P(V^\vee)$ defined by a basis of $V$ is a closed immersion with $\varphi_{\mathcal L,V}^*\mathcal O(1)\cong\mathcal L$ [def-weil-pbc-morphism-to-projective-space-by-sections] [def-pc-projective-space-twist]. In particular, if $V=H^0(X,\mathcal L)$, the complete linear system is a closed immersion and $\mathcal L$ is very ample [def-sc-ample].

source.place: Tag 0E8S, lemma-separate-points-tangent-vectors (Lemma 33.23.1), statement and proof; finite-dimensionality of V is the proper coherent cohomology theorem, Tag 02O5, Proposition 30.19.1; hypothesis (0) (V generates L) is added to the statement of Tag 0E8S (E7): without it the lemma fails when X has a single closed point (X=Spec k, V=0), and the Stacks proof's 'Condition (1) implies that the elements of V generate L' needs a second closed point

proof.text: Proper coherent cohomology makes H^0(X,L) finite-dimensional; transport along H.zeroLinearEquiv with its k-linear structure, then use that a submodule of a finite-dimensional vector space is finite-dimensional.

For each closed x, the sections whose germs lie in m_x L_x form a k-submodule of V. If all basis vectors vanished there, their span would be this submodule, contradicting hypothesis (0). The union of their generating loci contains every closed point, hence is X: a nonempty closed complement in the compact T0 space X contains a closed point. At each stalk, an invertible-module trivialization turns a nonvanishing basis vector into a unit, so these germs span. Apply the stalk-span characterization of generating sections.

Construct the coordinate morphism phi from the generating basis. Use the existing generatingSections_pair theorem from CompleteLinearSystemClosed, now public, for the section-preserving isomorphism phi^* O(1) = L. Its existing native-chart comparison remains private in that module; no complete-linear-system closedness theorem is used. On a standard chart every section t in V is the coordinate ratio sum_i c_i T_i/T_j times the generating basis section s_j; this is map_eq_linearRatio_smul in the adopted library. Consequently its nonvanishing locus on that chart is the inverse image of the basic open of this ratio. Hypothesis (1) therefore makes phi injective on closed points.

source.place: Tag 0E8S; constructions.tex Tags 01N8 and 01NE, standard-chart formulas

proof.text: The coordinate map is proper because its composite to the separated projective target base is proper. Closed-point injectivity gives empty or singleton fibres over closed points. Projective space is locally Noetherian; the proper finite-fibre neighbourhood theorem makes phi finite on a neighbourhood of every closed target point. These opens cover the compact T0 target, since a nonempty closed complement would contain a closed point. Thus phi is finite.

source.place: Tag 0E8S, proper finite-fibre step; coherent.tex Tag 02OH

proof.text: At a closed x, Nullstellensatz identifies both residue fields with k, and the residue map of phi is bijective by composition with the structure map. For a tangent vector theta killed by the differential, the explicit formula for schemeTangentMap and its zero show theta followed by phi factors through the residue-field point of phi(x). Choose a standard chart containing phi(x). A section t in V vanishing at x is a ratio r times its generating coordinate section, and r evaluates to zero at phi(x). The factorization implies theta pulls this ratio back to zero. The preimage of the chart under theta is the whole dual-number spectrum because it contains its closed point. Naturality and scalar compatibility of section pullback now show theta^*t = 0. Adjunction uniqueness identifies this with the tensor-pullback unit in hypothesis (2), contradicting tangent separation for nonzero theta. Thus the differential is injective, and rational tangent-cotangent duality gives cotangent surjectivity.

The rational unramified cotangent criterion supplies an unramified source neighbourhood of every closed x. These neighbourhoods cover X by compactness and the closed-point argument. Unramifiedness is local at the source, so phi is unramified.

For a closed target point with singleton fibre {x}, the residue-field map is surjective, hence purely inseparable. The finite unramified one-point criterion gives a target neighbourhood on which phi is a closed immersion. For an empty fibre use the complement of the closed image, on which the source is empty. The resulting target neighbourhoods cover all closed points, hence the entire target. Closed immersions are local at the target, so phi is a closed immersion.

The preceding construction works for every finite basis of V and supplies the required twist isomorphism. Choose a finite basis of V to witness very ampleness. This already follows for any generating separating V, and in particular proves the requested implication when V is the whole section space.

lean.statement: theorem point_tangent_separation_closed_immersion (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] (X : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsProper f] (L : X.Modules) [L.IsInvertible] (V : Submodule k ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop).hom).obj (L.val.obj (Opposite.op ⊤)))) (hgen : ∀ x : X, IsClosed ({x} : Set X) → ∃ s : V, x ∈ Scheme.Modules.nonvanishingLocus L s.val) (hpoint : ∀ x y : X, IsClosed ({x} : Set X) → IsClosed ({y} : Set X) → x ≠ y → ∃ s : V, x ∉ Scheme.Modules.nonvanishingLocus L s.val ∧ y ∈ Scheme.Modules.nonvanishingLocus L s.val) (htangent : ∀ x : X, IsClosed ({x} : Set X) → ∀ θ : schemeTangentSpace k X f x, θ ≠ 0 → ∃ s : V, x ∉ Scheme.Modules.nonvanishingLocus L s.val ∧ ((Classical.choose (Scheme.Modules.exists_tensorPullbackAdjunction θ.val)).unit.app L).val.app (Opposite.op ⊤) s.val ≠ 0) : FiniteDimensional k V ∧ (∀ (I : Type u) [Finite I] (b : Module.Basis I k V), ∃ s : I → L.sections, (∀ i, (s i).val (Opposite.op ⊤) = (b i).val) ∧ ∃ hs : Epi (L.freeHomEquiv.symm s), IsClosedImmersion (ProjectiveSpace.homOfGeneratingSections I f L s hs) ∧ Nonempty (ProjectiveSpace.twistRestrict (ProjectiveSpace.homOfGeneratingSections I f L s hs) 1 ≅ L)) ∧ (V = ⊤ → IsVeryAmple f L)
